candidates.term: The Horizon at the Year Gate
candidates.defline: The Horizon stands at your Year Gate, in plain view: your first home spent openly on people and on chances.
candidates.reading: You grew up in a family that spent on guests, gifts and new plans, and everyone who visited could see it. Because money moved freely in the house you grew up in, you learned to spot a chance quickly and to hold cash loosely. That ease with risk has served you well, and you still give faster than you keep.
candidates.teaser: Generosity was visible in your beginnings: a family that spent on people and chances. Money finds you through motion and strangers, rarely through sitting still.

domain_readings.Wealth: Money entered your story as movement: a family that spent on people and chances, fortune arriving through doors rather than vaults. You inherited the nose for openings and the light grip. Keep one anchored account beyond charm’s reach. The rest genuinely belongs in play.
domain_readings.Family: Your family line carries a generous gambler: a father figure or elder whose open hands taught you about range and its price. The family fortune moved, and so does yours. Honor the generosity by adding the one thing they skipped, the floor beneath it.

candidates.life_chapter: Your early chapter watched money move: generosity visible, fortunes fluid, opportunity treated as a family member. It gave you ease around risk that vault-raised people never learn. Expect openings to find you lifelong, and expect to need the anchor you were never handed.
candidates.relations: The open-handed elder is this seat’s person: a father or patron whose generosity, or its costly absence, taught you what open hands do. You repay the lesson by giving with structure. Provide the way they meant to. Deliberately.
candidates.turn_catalyst: Run thin, the doors stand unknocked: openings sensed, motion postponed. Travel somewhere on a hunch this season. Your luck commutes.
candidates.turn_friction: Run heavy, everything circulates: money, favors, attention, none of it settling. Anchor one asset this year and let it bore you.
candidates.shadow_line: Overloaded, generosity performs: giving seen becoming the point of giving.
candidates.health_line: Your vitality is circulatory: it rises in motion and pools in stillness. Move daily, travel seasonally, and the engine self-maintains.

Wealth.headline: You learned early that money is for moving.
Wealth.recognition: You spend on people and chances easily, and a good opening excites you more than a full account. Because money in your first home came and went in plain sight, you feel calm with risks that frighten more careful people. A store kept apart from your generosity is the thing you find hardest to build, and you know it.
Wealth.lived: As a child you watched money arrive in good months and go out on visitors and fresh ideas. By your teens you had a quick eye for a chance, and saving was something you had to teach yourself.

Family.headline: Your family taught you generosity, and its price.
Family.recognition: You give freely in your family, the treat paid for and the loan made without terms. Because an older relative showed you that generosity makes people love you, you find it hard to refuse anyone close. You keep giving after you can afford to, and you resent it only later.
Family.lived: An older relative in your first home, a parent or someone who stood in for one, spent widely and drew people around them. Growing up you learned both the warmth of that generosity and what it cost the household.
